title: Novel Hardware Architectures for PRESENT Block Cipher and its FPGA Realizations
problem: Lightweight cryptography for IoT faces challenges in power consumption and throughput. PRESENT cipher lacks comprehensive power-optimized hardware architectures despite being ideal for IoT applications.
motivation: IoT devices require lightweight ciphers balancing security, power efficiency, and hardware footprint. PRESENT is a 64-bit lightweight cipher, but existing implementations have not fully optimized power metrics while maintaining competitive throughput.
method: Novel hardware architectures for PRESENT cipher optimizing the Substitution Permutation Network (SPN) module via: (1) modified datapath design, (2) optimized input selection via multiplexers for substitution and permutation layers, (3) additional hardware units reducing power. Evaluated on NEXYS4 DDR FPGA at 13.56 MHz (RFID frequency).
key_novelty: Comprehensive power-optimized SPN module design for PRESENT cipher, achieving significant power reduction while maintaining high throughput and FPGA resource utilization.
contributions: 28.57% dynamic power reduction compared to state-of-the-art
Optimized SPN module input selection and feeding technique
Improved throughput while maintaining optimized energy consumption
Practical FPGA implementation at 13.56 MHz for IoT/RFID applications
Design guidelines for FPGA resource optimization in cipher architectures
limitations: FPGA-only implementation; ASIC synthesis results not provided
Limited to single frequency (13.56 MHz RFID band); scalability to higher frequencies not discussed
No power breakdown analysis (dynamic vs. static vs. leakage)
Throughput improvements not quantified in absolute terms
Limited comparison with other lightweight ciphers (AES-Tiny, SPECK, SIMON)
No formal security analysis or side-channel evaluation
